issue_context.title: should not return error when updating timestamp to an overflowed value with 'ignore'
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

```
> create table t(t timestamp);
> insert into t values("2000-01-01");
> update ignore t set t=cast("2099-01-01" as date);
> select * from t;
```

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

```
mysql> update ignore t set t=cast("2099-01-01" as date);
Query OK, 1 row affected, 1 warning (0.00 sec)
Rows matched: 1  Changed: 1  Warnings: 1

mysql> select * from t;
+---------------------+
| t                   |
+---------------------+
| 0000-00-00 00:00:00 |
+---------------------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec)
```

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

```
mysql> update ignore t set t=cast("2099-01-01" as date);
ERROR 1292 (22007): Incorrect timestamp value: '2099-01-01'
mysql> select * from t;
+---------------------+
| t                   |
+---------------------+
| 2000-01-01 00:00:00 |
+---------------------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec)
```

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

master
comments: Seeing the same issue on v5.4.0 as well.

@jebter 
This is not an inconsistency issue, but a MySQL compatible issue, the severity could be lowered.

review_comments:
Related error handling logic in Insert statement: 
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/47179ae14d6bb7947d8857b4e8c91212bce999aa/pkg/executor/insert_common.go#L324-L328

I've added error type and column type checking to avoid mishandling other errors here.

So the condition here allowed to be igmored is "timestamp column && truncated value", right?
Is this condition check consistent with MySQL behaviour?
